> 「世尊说我见、人见、众生见、寿者见，即非我见、人见、众生见、寿者见，是名我见……」「于一切法，应如是知，如是见，如是信解，不生法相。」

Section thirty-one moves the four marks from 相 to 见 — from marks to views.

我见、人见、众生见、寿者见: the view of a self, of a person, of a being, of a lifespan. Not the appearances this time, but the settled opinions about them.

And the formula applies to the views exactly as it applied to the marks: they are not views, therefore they are called views.

## 见 is not what the eyes do

见 here is a fixed conclusion — the mind's settled determination that there is a self, that there are others over against it, that beings persist, that there is a span of life to be lived and defended.

These are not errors of fact. They are the operating assumptions underneath nearly everything else, and they are remarkably hard to see because they do not present themselves as assumptions. They present themselves as the way things are.

## The instruction: 如是知，如是见，如是信解

Know thus. See thus. Understand and believe thus.

Thus — 如 — as it is. Which is not a content. There is no proposition to be substituted for the four views; the instruction is a mode of holding, not a replacement doctrine.

This is why the section is easy to read past. A reader expects the sutra to finally say what is true. Instead it says: hold it the way it is, and 不生法相 — do not give rise to a dharma-mark.

## 不生法相 is the last trap

The series of negations has one more exit, and this section closes it: the insight itself.

A person who has followed thirty sections has, by now, formed a view. Something like: everything is empty, marks are not ultimate, attachment is the problem. That view is now the most valuable thing the person owns — and 法相 means exactly this: a mark made of a dharma, a truth held as an object.

The book's line: this understanding can carry you across; on the far bank, the raft is left. The trouble is that most people carry the raft and call it humility.

## Why the four views are not to be destroyed

One more guardrail, and it is important.

The section does not say: eliminate the four views by force. They have no substance to eliminate. What is asked is to see them as conventional designations — useful, functioning, and not grounds.

Trying to destroy them builds a fifth view, subtler than the four: the view of one who has no views. The book calls this the most refined version of the same illness.

## The test

State your deepest conviction about how things are. One sentence, in your own words.

Then apply the formula: is this a 法相? Is it a truth you are holding — something whose loss would feel like a loss of yourself?

If yes, the section has done its work. The conviction may still be correct. It is simply, at this point, luggage.
